scope: Visible draft, deployed JSON, October 21 activity counts, fleet onboarding, October 20 review chain, Classic Space owner and research gates, action candidates and timing identity. Read-only review; no acceptance, action or scheduling authority.

findings.title: Deployed API reports 13 commits for a 31-commit window
findings.location: Frontmatter summary: “Thirty-one commits across three repos”; deployed JSON: `commitCount: 13`.
findings.explanation: Primary GitHub commit queries over the consecutive 03:30 Chicago cutoff interval return 19 core, 11 daily-logger and one morning-cockpit commit. Thirteen is the number of explicitly listed short SHAs, not the activity total.
findings.correction: Preserve 31 as the sourced activity count and make the API report 31, or relabel 13 as explicitly listed commit references.

findings.title: Fleet onboarding paragraph has wrong links and an impossible count
findings.location: Line 39: “surface 5 of 3 required surfaces” with morning-cockpit links for core #557, daily-logger #407 and core #542.
findings.explanation: The links target nonexistent pull requests in morning-cockpit and create three false unavailable timestamp controls. Daily-logger #407 documents surfaces 3 and 4; morning-cockpit #59 is a separate sibling, and no primary record supports 5 of 3.
findings.correction: Use the actual repositories for all three links and replace the contradictory ordinal with the documented onboarding walk or omit it.

findings.title: Merged review data already itemizes the ten October 20 errors
findings.location: Lines 28 and 71: “The specific nature of the ten errors is not itemized in the available commit record.”
findings.explanation: Merged PR #402 registers a full C1–C10 source-bound report with locations, evidence, corrections and open dispositions. PR #406 records their final resolution; the data is discoverable by the current article-review service.
findings.correction: Summarize or link the actual ten-finding taxonomy and preserve its source-pinned dispositions.

findings.title: PR #407 has review context and no admitted merge authority
findings.location: Lines 77 and 95–96: “No stated reviewer or hold was recorded” and “Merge ... No design work required.”
findings.explanation: An OWNER comment reviewed an earlier head, recorded one wording refinement for James's review and disclosed an omitted local typecheck. The PR later advanced; checks are green, but the article action review remains pending and no suggestion is admitted.
findings.correction: Record the bounded nonblocking review and exact head, keep final-head review and merge separate, and do not treat the pending candidate as merge authority.

findings.title: Fleet-runner ownership is recorded under core #307
findings.location: Lines 77 and 97: core #561 has “no named owner.”
findings.explanation: The #560 ruling explicitly assigns ownership to fleet-runner under core #307 and says review belongs there. #561 has no individual assignee or timeline, but that is different from no owner; its consumer review also records open contract gaps.
findings.correction: Name fleet-runner under core #307 as owner while separately stating that individual assignment, acceptance and timeline remain open.

findings.title: Research tickets are serialized and #567 already ran
findings.location: Lines 83 and 95: #543, #563 and #567 “can begin independently” and “proceed in parallel.”
findings.explanation: Issue #563 is serialized after #543; #567 is ordered before both and already records a landed Tier 0 cycle. The article says serialized while prescribing the opposite execution shape.
findings.correction: Preserve the recorded serial order and existing #567 result; do not admit or dispatch the #543 candidate from this review.

findings.title: Issue #357 is misidentified as the 4 a.m. timing candidate
findings.location: Lines 81 and 100: “The 4 a.m. public draft timing candidate (issue #357).”
findings.explanation: #357 is the article-review surface and current correspondence/evidence target. The timing candidate is a separate retained local proposal; #408 leaves the 4 a.m. fallback and earlier public-delivery adoption to a separate owner decision.
findings.correction: Keep #357 as the review-surface identity, refer to the timing proposal by its own retained identity, and keep start and public-availability goals separately unproven.

findings.title: Blender's world-hub role does not settle the authoritative geometry source
findings.location: Line 53: “established Blender as the authoritative geometry authoring surface.”
findings.explanation: The ruling puts Blender in the pipeline, but #544 still asks what Blender authors and how it exports, while #551 still asks which source is authoritative and is blocked on #544 plus route proof.
findings.correction: State that Blender's participation and world-hub role are ruled while authored scope, export contract and authoritative spatial source remain HITL decisions.

findings.title: The historical rationale for choosing 03:30 is unsupported
findings.location: Lines 28 and 65: 03:30 was chosen “to clear the overnight processing window before the morning cockpit surface activates.”
findings.explanation: #408 proves the declared cutoff, DST-safe interval and guard, but not this historical rationale. Run #261 started at 04:02:17 Chicago after a 1,937-second delay and does not establish by-04:00 public availability.
findings.correction: Retain the declared cutoff and actual receipt; attribute the rationale only to a primary decision and keep start, completion, merge and public availability separate.

findings.title: The five-PR chain is not an adopted universal reference pattern
findings.location: Line 71: “first fully documented supervised correction train” and “now the reference pattern for future multi-finding corrections.”
findings.explanation: The five PRs and their order are real, but no reviewed ADR or process source adopts that exact sequence for future cycles. #404 was a source-specific runtime repair, not a universal stage.
findings.correction: Describe the observed October 20 sequence without promoting it to an adopted future pattern absent an explicit decision.
